chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, the cousin of Shahab ibn Abd Rabbah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Five [people] are waited for until their bodies change: the drowned, the struck by lightning, the bloated (from internal causes), the buried under ruins, and the choked with smoke.

key_terms.وَالْمَبْطُونُ: The one who died of internal bloating/swelling
key_terms.يَتَغَيَّرُوا: Until they change (referring to bodily decomposition)

ai.seo_question: Which five types of corpses should not be buried immediately according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s ruling that the corpses of the drowned, lightning-struck, bloated, buried under ruins, and smoke-choked must remain unburied until their physical state changes, primarily to distinguish them from others in shared graves or to confirm death. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on *takhalluf* (delaying burial) for specific natural causes, ensuring proper identification and honoring the distinct manner of their passing before interment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-75 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Yunus ibn Abdul-Rahman, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Abdul Khaliq ibn Akhi Shahab ibn Abdeh Rab’beh that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

Five people should not be buried until the condition of their body changes as follows: people who have been drowned; those who have been stricken by lightning; those who have died because of intestinal problems; those who have been buried under a building and those who have been choked with smoke.”
